political_system.type: Federal semi-presidential republic under strong executive dominance (Super-Presidential system)
political_system.executive: President of the Russian Federation is Head of State and Supreme Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces; commands supreme authority over foreign, security, and defense policy; appoints the Prime Minister and government ministers; constitutional amendments passed in 2020 allow the incumbent to serve until 2036.
political_system.legislature: Bicameral Federal Assembly: State Duma (450 seats elected via mixed system) and Federation Council (upper house composed of representatives from each of the 89 federal subjects).
political_system.judiciary: Centralized civil law system headed by the Constitutional Court and Supreme Court; politically subservient to executive governance in national security and political matters.
political_system.structure: Asymmetric federalism comprising 89 federal subjects (including annexed Ukrainian regions), including republics, krais, oblasts, autonomous okrugs, and federal cities (Moscow, St. Petersburg, Sevastopol).
political_system.election_system: Direct universal presidential election every 6 years; mixed-member majoritarian system for State Duma (half single-member districts, half proportional representation with a 5% threshold).

current_government.president: Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin (re-elected to fifth presidential term in March 2024)
current_government.defense_minister: Andrey Belousov (technocratic economist appointed to oversee defense industrial production and budget efficiency)
current_government.context: Complete consolidation of state, media, judicial, and security apparatus (Siloviki) behind the wartime national security strategy; systematic suppression of political opposition and anti-war dissent.

major_parties.name: United Russia (Yedinaya Rossiya)
major_parties.ideology: Putinism, conservative statism, Russian civilizational nationalism, social stability, strong military
major_parties.status: Ruling party holding constitutional supermajority in the State Duma

major_parties.name: Communist Party of the Russian Federation (CPRF)
major_parties.ideology: Socialism, Soviet patriotism, state ownership of natural resources, social welfare
major_parties.status: Systemic opposition party, largely supporting executive foreign policy

major_parties.name: Liberal Democratic Party of Russia (LDPR)
major_parties.status: Systemic opposition party fully supporting the war effort

major_parties.name: A Just Russia — For Truth (SRZP)
major_parties.ideology: Social democratic rhetoric, militarist patriotism, state interventionism
major_parties.status: Systemic opposition party aligned with executive military strategy

political_movements_and_dynamics.name: Wartime Keynesianism & Industrial Mobilization
political_movements_and_dynamics.description: Massive state expenditures directed into the military-industrial complex (defense spending exceeding 7% of GDP) driving industrial output, high wages for manufacturing and military enlistees, and regional wealth redistribution.
political_movements_and_dynamics.current_relevance: Maintains economic stability and domestic public acquiescence despite high inflation, labor shortages, and international sanctions.

political_movements_and_dynamics.name: Eurasian Civilizational Sovereignty
political_movements_and_dynamics.description: Official state ideology defining Russia not as a peripheral part of Europe, but as a unique, self-contained 'state-civilization' anchored in traditional values, Orthodox spirituality, and anti-colonial solidarity with the Global South.
political_movements_and_dynamics.current_relevance: Provides the ideological justification for decoupling from Western norms, international human rights treaties, and Western cultural institutions.

political_movements_and_dynamics.name: Siloviki Consolidation & Successional Continuity
political_movements_and_dynamics.description: Dominance of intelligence and security officials (FSB, SVR, GRU) throughout state ministries, state-owned corporations, and regional governorships.
political_movements_and_dynamics.current_relevance: Ensures unquestioned loyalty to supreme command, ruthless internal surveillance, and resilience against external regime-change attempts.

_meta.source: Constitution of the Russian Federation; Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation; Congressional Research Service (CRS Report R46761)
